## HeaderBar

Floating rounded app header bar: centered, at most 960px wide, 60px tall, `borderRadius.lg` and `shadow.md`. The bar's height plus its top margin is reserved in the layout, so nothing below it moves.

```tsx
import { HeaderBar, Button } from '@taein-ui/core';

<HeaderBar
  logo={<img src="/logo.svg" alt="Logo" />}
  title="My App"
  items={[
    { label: '홈', href: '/', active: true },
    { label: '소개', href: '/about' },
    { label: '문의', onClick: () => {} },
  ]}
  actions={<Button size="sm">로그인</Button>}
  sticky
/>
```

### Item forms (`navStyle`)

- `pill` (default): items sit in an outer pill as pill buttons. On mouse hover (touch is ignored) or keyboard focus a circle fills from below (`scale 0 → 1.2`), the label slides up out of the pill and a second label in the contrast color rises from below. Entering is `slow` `settle`, leaving is `base` `settle`, and a change mid-way continues from where it is. The `active` item is always in the filled end state (no motion on mount) and its covering label carries a still glow (`text-shadow`, same value as the Loader glow). When `active` moves to another item, the new one fills and the old one empties. Reduced motion: the end state appears at once.
- `text`: text links. On hover (`(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`) or keyboard focus a faint pill-shaped background (`currentColor` 10%, `fast` `settle`) appears behind the label. The `active` item always has that background and a semibold label. Reduced motion: no transition.
- `dropdown`: like `text`, but an item with `links` is an `aria-expanded` button with a chevron (it turns 180 degrees when open). A mouse entering the item opens a small panel below the bar, left-aligned with the item (`opacity 0 → 1`, `y 8 → 0`, `base` `settle`; closing `fast` `settle`) and leaving closes it; an invisible bridge above the panel keeps it open while the pointer crosses the gap. A mouse press only opens (it never closes a panel the hover opened). Touch, pen and keyboard (`Enter`/`Space`) press to open and press again to close. One panel is open at a time. It also closes on `Esc` (focus returns to the item), a press outside, a link press, or when focus leaves the panel. Below 768px the vertical list shows each item's links indented, always expanded.
- `cards`: the bar is the door. Items are not laid out inside the bar (they live only in the cards) and the hamburger shows at every width. Pressing it grows a surface behind the bar downward (`height` 60px → `max(260px, measured)` on wide screens, measured on narrow ones, `slow` `settle`) and the cards rise inside it (`y 50 → 0`, `opacity 0 → 1`, `slow` `settle`, 80ms apart, starting at 3/4 of the surface tween). Opening is `play()`, closing is `reverse()` (the cards sink first, then the surface shrinks), and reversing mid-way continues from where it is. The surface overlaps content instead of pushing it. Each item is a card; one with `links` is a `role="group"` labelled by its title and lists them below (`<a>` with `href`, otherwise `<button>`, an arrow in front), and one without `links` is itself the card's title link and not a group. Links in cards are at least 24px tall. Cards stack vertically below 768px. Prefer three cards or fewer. Closes on a second press, `Esc` (focus returns to the hamburger), a press outside the surface, or a link press. Reduced motion: opens to the end state and closes to the start at once.
- `icon`: icon pills where only the item under the pointer (or with keyboard focus) grows; its neighbors stay put. Hover and the `active` item get a faint `currentColor` background. Two guards keep it legible: items only ever grow from rest, and the hit area is a fixed `RESERVED_SIZE` (56px) box. Every item needs an `icon` (type error otherwise); `label` is the accessible name.

```tsx
import { HeaderBar } from '@taein-ui/core';
import { CircleCheck, Info, Plus } from 'lucide-react';

<HeaderBar
  title="My App"
  navStyle="icon"
  items={[
    { icon: <Info />, label: '홈', href: '/' },
    { icon: <Plus />, label: '새로 만들기', onClick: () => {} },
    { icon: <CircleCheck />, label: '완료함' },
  ]}
/>
```

### Narrow screens (below 768px)

The items hide and a hamburger button (two lines that gather into an X, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, name "메뉴 열기" / "메뉴 닫기") appears. It opens a vertical list panel below the bar (same width, corners and shadow; it overlaps content instead of pushing it). Opening fades and slides the panel in (`opacity 0 → 1`, `y 8 → 0`, `base` `settle`), closing is `fast` `settle`. `Esc` closes it and returns focus to the hamburger; pressing outside the panel or an item also closes it. Reduced motion: the panel appears and disappears at once.

### Props (extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, without `title` and `children`)
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| logo | ReactNode | - | Logo element |
| title | ReactNode | - | Title/heading |
| titleAs | 'h1' to 'h6' or 'span' | 'h1' | Element of the title, same style for every value. Use a lower level or `span` when the page already has an h1 |
| items | HeaderBarItem[] | - | Center items: `{ label, href?, onClick?, icon?, active?, links? }`. `<a>` with `href`, otherwise `<button>`; `active` sets `aria-current="page"`. With `navStyle="icon"` every item needs `icon`. `links` (`{ label, href?, onClick? }[]`) is used by `navStyle="dropdown"` and `"cards"` |
| navStyle | 'pill' \| 'text' \| 'dropdown' \| 'cards' \| 'icon' | 'pill' | How the items look |
| actions | ReactNode | - | Right side actions |
| sticky | boolean | false | Sticks to the top of the viewport (keeps its top margin) |
| aria-label | string | - | Accessibility label |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class |

---

## HangulAssemble

Sentence whose Hangul syllables assemble from pieces of the rendered syllable when it scrolls into view. Each syllable is cut into initial, medial and final regions (ㅎ, ㅏ, ㄴ of 한; initial left or top, vowel right or below, final at the bottom); the pieces are copies of the finished syllable clipped to those regions, so they have the same font, size and color. They fly in from scattered places (60 to 120px away, slightly tilted) and interlock one cell after another (60ms apart); the moment the last piece lands the finished syllable shows, with no cross-fade. Characters that are not Hangul syllables (Latin, digits, punctuation, a lone jamo) only fade in, in the same order. Spaces are kept as they are.

```tsx
import { HangulAssemble } from '@taein-ui/core';

<HangulAssemble text="안녕하세요" as="h1" />
<HangulAssemble text="TaeinUI로 만든 한글 문장" className="hero" ref={ref} />
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| text | string | (required) | Sentence to show. Changing it does not replay: the new sentence appears finished |
| as | 'h1' \| 'h2' \| 'h3' \| 'h4' \| 'h5' \| 'h6' \| 'p' \| 'span' \| 'div' | 'p' | Root element |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class |
| ref | Ref<HTMLElement> | - | Forwarded to the root element |

There is no `size` or `variant`: the type size comes from the root element's own font. It takes no other props.

### Behavior
- The first render (SSR included) is the finished sentence. The scattered start state is applied only just before playback, in a client effect, after the root's font has loaded (`document.fonts.load`, at most 3 seconds; skipped when `document.fonts` is missing). The first render stays the finished sentence while it waits. Mounted already on screen: it plays at once, before the first paint. Mounted below the fold: it waits, hides when `IntersectionObserver` reports it is off screen, plays once when it scrolls in, then stops observing.
- Reduced motion, or an environment without `IntersectionObserver`: nothing is hidden, the finished sentence is shown. Printing always shows the finished sentence.
- Accessibility: the root holds one visually hidden copy of `text` (read as the sentence) and an `aria-hidden` visual layer. The root has no `aria-label`. Each word is `white-space: nowrap`, so a Korean word is never split at a line end.
- Motion: piece flight `slower` `settle`, pieces of one syllable shifted by `fast` * 0.2 (30ms), start of each cell shifted by `fast` * 0.4 (60ms), narrowed for long sentences so the last cell starts within 1 second of the first. The scattered positions are fixed by character index (no randomness), so they are the same on every render.

---

## BrushText

Sentence written as if by a brush when it scrolls into view. At playback the finished syllable of each cell is drawn to a canvas with the same font and color, the ink pixels are measured, and each connected blob of ink (8-neighbour) is found as a stroke. Tiny blobs (under 0.2% of the cell, brush splinters) are attached to the nearest stroke. Each stroke is given to a jamo by where its centre falls in the jamo regions of the syllable (ㅎ, ㅏ, ㄴ of 한; the same regions as HangulAssemble). A blob that a brush font draws across two or more jamo regions (ㄷ+ㅗ of 독, ㄴ+ㅣ of 니) is split first: pixels are sorted into the regions, and when two or more regions each hold a large share of the blob, the remaining pixels join the nearest of those pixels inside the blob, so each jamo gets its own part. The jamo are written in order (initial, vowel, final), and within a jamo the strokes go from top to bottom by their start point (left to right at the same height), which gives the usual Hangul stroke order for ㅗ, ㅜ and ㅏ. The brush front moves along each stroke by geodesic distance inside the blob from its upper left start, so a bent stroke (ㄱ, ㄹ) is drawn along its bend. The front is a hard edge about 0.04em wide with a steady speed. There is no blur, bleed or fade: the brush texture comes from the font. When the last stroke of a syllable ends, its canvas is removed from view and the finished syllable (real text) is all that is left. Non-Hangul characters (Latin, digits, punctuation, a lone jamo) are one blob each, written from the left. Spaces are kept as they are and take no time.

It does not carry a font: it uses the parent's `font-family`. A brush font such as Nanum Brush Script (OFL) looks best, but the motion is the same with any font. A blob where a font joins neighbouring jamo is split by the share of its pixels in each jamo region and written jamo by jamo. The font has no stroke information, so a long stroke lying across a region border can be split in part. It is for a short line such as a hero sentence or a section title, not for long paragraphs: every syllable is drawn and measured at playback and the pixels of the stroke being written are redrawn each frame. Playback waits until the element is on screen.

```tsx
import { BrushText } from '@taein-ui/core';

<BrushText text="붓으로 쓰듯 나타납니다" as="h1" />
<BrushText text="TaeinUI로 쓴 한글 문장" className="hero" ref={ref} />
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| text | string | (required) | Sentence to write. Changing it does not replay: the new sentence appears finished |
| as | 'h1' \| 'h2' \| 'h3' \| 'h4' \| 'h5' \| 'h6' \| 'p' \| 'span' \| 'div' | 'p' | Root element |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class |
| ref | Ref<HTMLElement> | - | Forwarded to the root element |

There is no `size` or `variant`: the type size and the font come from the root element's own style. It takes no other props.

### Behavior
- The first render (SSR included) is the finished sentence. The hidden start state is applied only just before playback, in a client effect, after the root's font has loaded (`document.fonts.load`, at most 3 seconds; skipped when `document.fonts` is missing). The first render stays the finished sentence while it waits. Mounted already on screen: it plays at once, before the first paint. Mounted below the fold: it waits, hides when `IntersectionObserver` reports it is off screen, plays once when it scrolls in, then stops observing.
- Reduced motion, or an environment without `IntersectionObserver`: nothing is hidden, the finished sentence is shown. Printing always shows the finished sentence.
- Accessibility: the root holds one visually hidden copy of `text` (read as the sentence) and an `aria-hidden` visual layer. The root has no `aria-label`. Each word is `white-space: nowrap`, so a Korean word is never split at a line end.
- Without a usable canvas (no 2D context, no font metrics) nothing is hidden and the finished sentence is shown.
- Motion: a stroke takes `base` (200ms) per em of its length (a 0.5em stroke is 100ms), at least `fast` * 0.4 (60ms), `linear`. The brush lifts for `fast` * 0.4 (60ms) between strokes of one jamo, `base` * 0.5 (100ms) between jamo and `fast` (150ms) between syllables. There is no cap on the total length: a long sentence takes as long as it takes.

---

## GooeySearch

Round search button that splits like a water drop: pressing it pulls a second blob off to the right and the input stretches out between the two, revealed along the growing pill with a `clip-path`. Closing merges the blobs back. The pill takes 600ms and the ball 750ms (`slower` x 1.2 and x 1.5) with `drift`; an SVG goo filter (blur plus alpha threshold) joins the shapes while they are close. When the reveal ends the input takes focus (immediately under reduced motion).

Controlled: you hold `open`. `onOpenChange(next, event?)` is called for the trigger click, for Esc (keydown on the document) and for a pointerdown outside the component, and the DOM event that caused it is the second argument, so a consumer can ignore some of them (for example synthetic pointer events in a scripted demo). Esc also moves focus back to the trigger. The component holds no input value: pass `value`, `onChange` and the rest through `inputProps`, and put the result list in `children`. Under reduced motion it opens and closes without splitting.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { GooeySearch } from '@taein-ui/core';

const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
const [query, setQuery] = useState('');

<GooeySearch
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={(next) => {
    setOpen(next);
    if (!next) setQuery('');
  }}
  placeholder="Search components..."
  inputProps={{ value: query, onChange: (e) => setQuery(e.target.value) }}
>
  {query && <ResultList query={query} />}
</GooeySearch>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| open | boolean | (required) | Whether the search is open |
| onOpenChange | (next: boolean, event?: Event) => void | (required) | Called with the next state and the DOM event that caused it |
| triggerRef | Ref<HTMLButtonElement> | - | Forwarded to the trigger button (for a keyboard shortcut to focus or click) |
| openLabel | string | '검색 열기' | Accessible name of the trigger while closed |
| closeLabel | string | '검색 닫기' | Accessible name of the trigger while open |
| inputLabel | string | '검색' | Accessible name of the input |
| placeholder | string | - | Placeholder of the input |
| inputProps | InputHTMLAttributes (without id, type, className, aria-label, placeholder) | - | Native attributes for the input: value, onChange, onKeyDown, role, aria-* |
| children | ReactNode | - | Result list, placed below the input |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class. Width and placement are yours to set |
| ref | Ref<HTMLDivElement> | - | Forwarded to the root element |

### Accessibility
- The trigger is a button named by `openLabel` / `closeLabel` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the input. Put a shortcut hint in the name (for example 'Open search (Ctrl K)').
- The input is `inert` while closed, so it is not reachable by keyboard or screen reader.
- Focus is drawn on the control itself, not as an outer ring: the open input gets a 2px `primary` border inside its edge (`:focus`, a mouse click too), and the round trigger gets a white inner band while keyboard-focused (`:focus-visible`).
- Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger, unless something inside (for example a combobox in `children`) already handled that Esc with `preventDefault()`. Selecting a result and where focus goes afterwards is yours to handle.
- The combobox wiring is the consumer's: pass `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant` and the arrow/Enter keys through `inputProps`, and give the result list the matching roles.

---

## CopyButton

Copy button for one string. Pressing it writes `value` with `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. On success the clipboard icon folds into a check (the check's lines draw in) and the label slides up out of the way while the copied label rises from below; after `loop.base` (1500ms) everything runs back. If `navigator.clipboard` is missing (an insecure context) or rejects the write, the icon shakes sideways (the same keyframes and tokens as the TextField error shake) and the label becomes the failed label, then returns. The three labels share one grid cell, so the button keeps its width in every state.

It wraps `Button` (`variant="light"`, the outline look, `md` size), so it keeps the press and hover feel of `Button`. It has no `size` or `variant` prop.

```tsx
import { CopyButton } from '@taein-ui/core';

<CopyButton value="pnpm add @taein-ui/core" />
<CopyButton value={url} label="링크 복사" copiedLabel="복사됨" failedLabel="복사 실패" onCopy={(ok) => track(ok)} />
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| value | string | (required) | Text to copy |
| label | string | '복사' | Resting label and the button's accessible name in every state |
| copiedLabel | string | '복사됨' | Label after a successful copy |
| failedLabel | string | '복사 실패' | Label after a failed copy |
| onCopy | (ok: boolean) => void | - | Called with the result. Not called when `onClick` calls `preventDefault()` or the button is disabled. (This replaces the native clipboard `onCopy`, which is not accepted) |
| disabled | boolean | false | Disabled state; nothing is copied |
| onClick | MouseEventHandler | - | Runs before the copy. `event.preventDefault()` skips the copy |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the `<button>`) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLButtonElement> | - | Forwarded to the `<button>` |

Other native button attributes are passed to the `<button>`, except `children`, `value` and `onCopy`.

### Accessibility
- The accessible name is always `label`; the name does not change after a copy. The other two labels are `aria-hidden`.
- A visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` region (`role="status"`) next to the button reads the copied or failed label once, and is emptied when the button returns to rest.
- Pressing again while the copied or failed label shows copies again and restarts the timer. Each press renders a fresh node inside the region, so the result is read again.
- The timer is cleared on unmount.
- Reduced motion: the icon and the label only cross-fade. No sliding, rotating, line drawing or shake.

---

## BurstToggle

Toggle button for like, save and favorite. Turning it on, the icon squashes flat (about 0.7 tall and 1.15 wide), springs past 1.2x and settles back to 1, and at the same moment it swaps to the selected icon while a ring of 8 small dots in the `primary` color bursts outward from the icon center, shrinking and fading. Turning it off quietly swaps to the off icon with a small press and no dots. The state is yours (a controlled component, like `Chip`'s `selected`).

The filled look is made by swapping two icons, not by giving an outline icon a fill. The icon cell is the `IconButton` `md` size and the icon `svg` is `1em`. It has no `size` or `variant` prop.

```tsx
import { BurstToggle } from '@taein-ui/core';
import { Heart } from 'lucide-react';

<BurstToggle
  aria-label="좋아요"
  selected={liked}
  onClick={() => setLiked(!liked)}
  selectedIcon={<Heart fill="currentColor" />}
>
  <Heart />
</BurstToggle>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| selected | boolean | (required) | On state. Announced with `aria-pressed` |
| selectedIcon | ReactNode | (required) | Icon shown while on |
| children | ReactNode | (required) | Icon shown while off |
| aria-label | string | (required) | Accessible name, the same in both states |
| onClick | MouseEventHandler | - | Native click. Flip your state here. `preventDefault()` there skips the burst and the press squash |
| disabled | boolean | false | Disabled state; `onClick` is not called |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the `<button>`) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLButtonElement> | - | Forwarded to the `<button>` |

Other native button attributes are passed to the `<button>`, except `children` and `aria-pressed`.

### Behavior
- The burst happens only when this button's own click goes from off to on. A `selected` that is already true on mount, or that changes from outside without a click, does not burst.
- The burst plays in the render where `selected` actually becomes true after this button's click. If your `onClick` refuses the change (login needed, rejected), nothing bursts.
- Known limit: after a refused click, the button keeps its "waiting for the turn-on" mark until the next click or until `selected` turns on. If `selected` is turned on from outside in between, the dots burst once. A late turn-on after an async confirmation looks the same, so the two cannot be told apart.
- Pressing again while the burst runs turns it off and clears the remaining dots at once.
- The dots are `aria-hidden` decoration. They exist only while the burst runs and leave the DOM when it ends. The button has `overflow: visible`, so they are not clipped, and they are absolutely placed, so they never push the layout.

### Accessibility
- A `<button>` with `aria-pressed` and a fixed `aria-label`; the icons are `aria-hidden`.
- Reduced motion: only the icon swaps. No squash, spring or dots.

---

## HoldButton

Hold-to-confirm button for things that cannot be undone (delete, pay, reset). Press and hold: the inside fills with `primary.main` (blue) from the left, and the text turns white where the fill has passed over 1.5 seconds, the last 30% trembles 1 to 2px with growing swing, and when it is full a check springs in and `onConfirm` is called. Letting go early drains the fill back (`base`, `settle`).

There is also a path that does not depend on time (WCAG 2.1.1; screen readers and voice control send one click). A short press, a keyboard tap or one click only **arms** the button: the label becomes `confirmLabel`, the fill rests at half and a `role="status"` region announces it. The next click calls `onConfirm`. Arming has no timer; it is released when focus leaves the button. Safari and Firefox on macOS and iOS Safari do not focus a button on a mouse click or a tap, so after arming with those inputs, clicking elsewhere does not release it.

It wraps `Button` `light` (`md`), so it keeps the height, radius, press and hover feel of `Button`. The white text is an `aria-hidden` copy of the text laid over the button and clipped to the same progress value as the fill. If `disabled` turns on during a hold, the hold is dropped and `onConfirm` is not called. It has no `size` or `variant` prop and no hold-time prop: the hold is fixed at 1.5 seconds (`gsapDuration.slower` x 3) so it cannot be tuned down to nothing.

```tsx
import { HoldButton } from '@taein-ui/core';

<HoldButton onConfirm={deleteAll} confirmLabel="한 번 더 누르면 삭제">삭제</HoldButton>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| children | ReactNode | (required) | Button text and the resting accessible name |
| onConfirm | () => void | (required) | Runs when the hold completes, and on the second click of the armed path. Called once per run |
| confirmLabel | string | '한 번 더 누르면 실행' | Label while armed (also the accessible name then, and what the status region announces) |
| disabled | boolean | false | Disabled state; no path runs `onConfirm` |
| onClick | MouseEventHandler | - | Native click. **Not** a confirmation: a click is produced every time a press ends, so do not run the action here |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the `<button>`) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLButtonElement> | - | Forwarded to the `<button>` |

Other native button attributes are passed to the `<button>`, except `children` and `type`. `type` is always `button`: a `submit` button would submit the form on the arming click. To submit a form, call `form.requestSubmit()` in `onConfirm`.

### Behavior
- Holding starts on pointerdown or on Space or Enter keydown (a repeated keydown is ignored). pointerup, pointercancel, pointerleave and keyup drain it back.
- Letting go during a hold also produces a click. That click arms the button, and the fill drains to half and rests there.
- When the hold completes it runs once and the click that follows is ignored.
- After running, a `role="status"` region says it is done and the button becomes `aria-disabled` (focus stays). It returns to rest after 2 seconds and cannot run again meanwhile.

### Accessibility
- The hold-and-fill path is never the only path: one click arms and a second click runs, so keyboard, screen reader and voice users are not asked to hold anything for a length of time.
- The accessible name is `children` at rest and `confirmLabel` while armed. A visually hidden `role="status"` region announces the armed and the done states.
- Reduced motion: the hold time is unchanged (shortening it would run the action at once). The fill grows in four steps instead of continuously; there is no tremble and no spring.

---

## SloshGauge

Display meter for a value such as storage, quota or progress (`role="meter"`). A drop-shaped bowl (pointed top, round bottom, `primary` outline) holds water whose surface height is the value. The level is by area, not height: 50% fills half of the bowl's area, so the surface sits below the middle of its height.

When `value` changes the level behaves like a spring: it overshoots the target by 10 to 25% and is calm within about 1.5 seconds after a big change. The surface tilts with the level's speed (an increase lifts the left side first, up to 15 to 20 degrees at the peak) under two sine waves: a front one with a `primary` gradient that darkens with depth and a light rim, and a translucent back one in another phase. A few bubble rings (at most 8, about 3 to 8px) rise from the bottom only while it shakes hard, and none remain at rest. The bowl itself tips by about 1 degree and stretches by under 1% on a big change, then straightens. A slim gloss runs down the inside of its left wall.

The shake is read from the current level speed and tilt, so it does not pile up when the value keeps changing (a download updating every 100ms), and a change in the middle of a slosh continues from the current level without a jump.

At rest a slow, low ripple (about 1 to 2% of the bowl height) always remains. Because that moves for more than 5 seconds, `paused` is the pause control (WCAG 2.2.2). Drawing also stops while the tab is hidden or the bowl is off screen.

```tsx
import { SloshGauge } from '@taein-ui/core';

<SloshGauge value={60} label="저장 공간" valueText="6GB / 10GB" />

// freeze the water (for a pause button or a "stop motion" switch)
<SloshGauge value={60} label="저장 공간" paused={frozen} />
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| value | number | (required) | Current value. Clipped to `min`..`max` |
| min | number | 0 | Bottom of the range |
| max | number | 100 | Top of the range |
| label | string | (required) | Accessible name and the visible caption under the bowl |
| valueText | string | - | Visible value text and `aria-valuetext`. Percentage ("60%") when absent |
| paused | boolean | false | `true` freezes the water as it is (no animation loop). A value change then sets the level at once with no slosh. `false` continues from the frozen look |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the root) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLDivElement> | - | Forwarded to the root |

Other native div attributes are passed to the root, except `children` and `role`. The width is set by the parent (7.5rem by default); the bowl keeps its own ratio. There is no `size` or `variant`.

### Accessibility
- The root is `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow` (the new value at once, not after the animation), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuetext` and `aria-labelledby` (the visible `label`).
- The bowl and the water are `aria-hidden` decoration.
- The bowl outline and the water fill are at least 3:1 against the background; the value text is at least 4.5:1.
- The resting ripple moves for more than 5 seconds, so it can be stopped with `paused` (WCAG 2.2.2).
- Reduced motion: the surface is flat with no ripple, and a value change only moves the level at once.

---

## CodeSlots

One-time code and PIN input (a form component: `label` is required). The real input is a single `<input>` laid transparently over the slots (not `display: none`), so focus, paste and one-time-code autofill land on it near the slots. The slots are `aria-hidden` pictures of its value.

- Typing a digit rolls it into its slot from above (`translateY(-100%)` to 0 with a slight overshoot, `base`, `snap`). Deleting drops the digit out below.
- `error`: the slots shake one after another from the left (the same kind of keyframes and tokens as the TextField error shake, `slower` and `drift`, but ±4px to fit the 8px gap; a stagger of `fast` x 0.3 per slot) and the borders turn `error`.
- `success`: the slots merge into one pill in two beats. First (`base`, `settle`) each slot's border and white fill fade out together while one bundle behind the slots (white fill plus a `success.dark` border, `aria-hidden`) fades in, so no slot keeps a white face of its own. Then (`slower`, `settle`) the slots close the gap to 0 and the bundle's real width shrinks with them (no `scale`, so its round ends never squash) while its corners round up to the pill radius; the bundle clips anything outside its rounded corners. Turning `success` off runs the same path back (second beat first, then the first), and a change mid-way reverses from the current shape, so the end shape always matches the last value. The border is `success.dark` (`success.main` is 2.77:1 on white).
- Focus is shown by border color, not an outer ring: while the input has focus, the slot to type into next (the last slot when full) gets a `primary` border (a mouse click does the same), and `error` wins over focus. Once merged the slots are transparent, so the bundle's `success.dark` border keeps its color and thickens from 1px to 2px while the input has focus (no ring is added; it eases with `fast` and `settle`, and changes at once under reduced motion). A slot that is disabled while focused keeps its disabled color.

```tsx
import { CodeSlots } from '@taein-ui/core';

<CodeSlots
  label="인증번호"
  length={6}
  value={code}
  onChange={setCode}
  onComplete={verify}
  error={wrong}
  errorMessage="번호가 맞지 않습니다"
  success={ok}
  successMessage="확인했습니다"
/>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| label | string | (required) | Accessible name and visible label |
| length | number | 6 | Number of slots |
| value | string | - | Controlled value. Digits only |
| defaultValue | string | - | Initial value (uncontrolled) |
| onChange | (value: string) => void | - | Receives the digits-only value |
| onComplete | (value: string) => void | - | Called once when `length` digits are in |
| helperText | string | - | Helper text |
| error | boolean | false | Error state. Wave and `error` borders; `aria-invalid="true"` |
| errorMessage | string | - | Shown instead of `helperText` while `error` |
| success | boolean | false | Success state. The slots merge into one pill. `error` wins when both are on |
| successMessage | string | - | Shown instead of `helperText` while `success` |
| disabled | boolean | false | Disables input |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the root) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLInputElement> | - | Forwarded to the hidden input |

Other native input attributes (`name`, `autoFocus`, `required`) are passed to the input, except `type`, `size`, `id`, `style`, `maxLength`, `inputMode`, `pattern`, `autoComplete`, `onSelect` and `children`. The input has `inputMode="numeric"`, `autoComplete="one-time-code"`, `maxLength={length}` and `pattern="\d*"`. Characters that are not digits are dropped; a paste is filtered to its digits, so "123 456" fills 123456. A paste of `length` digits or more replaces the whole value (a new code, so it never gets appended to a half-typed one); a shorter piece is appended to the current value and cut at `length`. The caret always stays at the end (no editing inside), so delete with Backspace from the end. There is no `size` or `variant`.

### Accessibility
- The accessible name is `label`; `helperText`, `errorMessage` and `successMessage` are tied to the input by `aria-describedby`, and the message is visible text, so error and success do not rely on motion or color alone.
- `aria-invalid="true"` while `error`.
- The slots are `aria-hidden`; the hidden input is the only focus stop.
- Reduced motion: no roll, drop, wave or merge transition. Digits and colors change at once and the merged shape appears in its end state.

---

## FanMenu

Radial action menu for quick actions and share menus (a menu button). A `primary` hub with a plus sits at the centre; pressing it springs the `items` out along an upper half circle.

- Open: the items come out one after another (45ms apart, `fast` x 0.3) along a half circle of radius 104px, from 180 degrees on the left to 0 on the right, from a small size to full size (`slower`, `snap`, transform only). The plus turns into a cross (135deg). A dotted guide arc appears and a `primary` glowing line is drawn along it (`stroke-dashoffset`, `slower` x 1.6, `settle`).
- Close: the reverse order, 30ms apart (`fast` x 0.2).
- Pointing (fine pointer only: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`): the icon nearest the angle from the hub centre to the pointer grows to 1.38x, moves 14px outward, fills `primary` and shows a name tag. Tracked only 36 to 230px from the centre; angles below the arc snap to the nearer end. Touch has no direction tracking: the pressed icon is chosen.
- Choosing an item calls `onSelect` once, flashes (375ms, `settle`) and folds; focus returns to the hub.

```tsx
import { FanMenu } from '@taein-ui/core';
import { Image, MessageCircle, Music } from 'lucide-react';

<FanMenu
  label="빠른 작업"
  items={[
    { icon: <Image />, label: '사진', onSelect: pickPhoto },
    { icon: <MessageCircle />, label: '메시지', onSelect: openChat },
    { icon: <Music />, label: '음악', onSelect: openMusic },
  ]}
/>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| label | string | (required) | Accessible name of the hub button. Fixed whether open or not; `aria-expanded` tells the state |
| items | { icon: ReactNode; label: string; onSelect: () => void }[] | (required) | 2 to 8 items. Outside that range a development warning is logged once and only the first 8 are drawn |
| disabled | boolean | false | Disables the hub |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the root) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLButtonElement> | - | Forwarded to the hub button |

Other native button attributes are passed to the hub, except `children`, `type` and `onSelect`. Open state is internal (there is no controlled prop). The fan always opens upward and does nothing about screen edges: the consumer leaves room (about 130px above and to each side of the hub). There is no `size` or `variant`.

### Accessibility
- Menu button pattern: the hub has `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the items are in `role="menu"` (named after the hub) as `role="menuitem"` with roving tabindex. The menu is `inert` while closed and while closing, so closed items are not in the tab order or the accessibility tree.
- Opening with Enter, Space or ArrowUp focuses the first item; opening with the mouse keeps focus on the hub.
- All four arrow keys move along the arc (wrapping at the ends); Home and End go to the ends. Esc folds and returns focus to the hub. Tab moving focus out of the menu folds it, and so does a mousedown outside. While the hub has focus the items are not in the tab order; ArrowUp enters them.
- A focused icon grows and shows its tag like a pointed one. The tag is an `aria-hidden` decoration (the item's accessible name is its `label`), closes with Esc, stays when the pointer moves onto it and never disappears on its own (WCAG 1.4.13).
- Items are 44px, at least 24x24, and do not overlap.
- Reduced motion: no stagger, guide drawing or flash. Items appear and disappear in place at once, and the pointed icon grows without a size transition.

---

## RocketButton

Send or submit button that launches like a rocket (a mail "Send" button). Pressing it crouches the button slightly down-left (`translate(-2px, 2px) scale(0.97)`, `fast`; it rewinds on `pointerleave` or `pointercancel`). When the native click is confirmed, a decorative copy of the button is lifted onto a fixed layer at the same screen rectangle and follows one beat function of the time (the button position and tilt, the jet strength and wick length, and the smoke are all taken from this one beat):
1. Nozzles out (0-600ms): the two nozzles slide down out of the button's lower border. They sit behind the button's body (lower in the stacking order, no clipping box), so they only show as far as they have come out and never above the body. No jet light or smoke yet.
2. Build-up (600-2600ms): the jet strength rises slowly from zero: a short wick and layered halos (a glow, not a long flame) light up under each nozzle. Smoke piles up on the virtual ground below the button (the place where the button stood, 34px below the nozzle mouths) and rolls sideways, and an exhaust column runs from each nozzle down to the ground, wider toward the bottom. The button stays in place.
3. Launch (2600-5100ms): thrust grows, so it lifts off heavily and slowly, accelerates, then curves slowly to the right. The tilt follows the direction of its velocity (at most 20deg). The virtual ground stays at the same height during the flight: the jet keeps making smoke where it reaches the ground right below the rocket, weaker the higher it is, and a weaker trail comes from under the nozzles. The exhaust column gets longer as the rocket climbs and thinner, and is gone when the flight ends. It leaves the screen (or the `container`).
4. End (5100ms): the mark fades in (`base`, `settle`).

The motion is a physical model (a growing thrust), not an easing curve, taken as a deterministic function of the time (the tremble and the flicker are sines, no random numbers), so the same time gives the same picture.

The two nozzles (small blobs at 30% of the button width on each side of the center, about 14x8px for a 44px button, rounder at the bottom, dark grey fading darker downward) are plain DOM inside the copy, behind the body, so they tilt and shrink with it. Each has a thin flat mouth (about 7x2px) whose color mixes from grey to the jet color (a light primary step) with the jet strength and that throws a small glow below. The jet is a glow, not a long stream: a short wick under the mouth (0.2 to 0.5 times the button height depending on the strength, flickering by +-10% as a fast deterministic function of the time; white in the middle, the jet color outside, a bell-shaped cross section that thins downward) inside layered halos of different radii (about 5px dense, 18px thin, 70px very faint). A faint light also rises from the body's underside (a decorative layer over the body, at most 30% and only in the lowest third so the text contrast stays above 4.5:1). One CSS custom property, `--rocket-thrust` (0 to 1, the beat function's jet strength, set every frame), drives the mouth color, the glow, the underside light and the DOM fallback light; the wick length changes only through `transform: scaleY`, so no layout property is touched per frame. Colors come from tokens only.

A WebGL2 fluid smoke in white rolls sideways on the virtual ground under the nozzles (about every 100ms, rarer the higher the rocket is) from the build-up to the end of the flight, and trails weakly from under the nozzles during the launch, in the direction of the button's underside. It has light and shade: the density gradient gives the surface direction, faces toward the upper-left light are the white token, shaded faces, parts thick toward the light and deep parts lean to `gray[400]`. The same canvas draws the jet glow (the wick and the halos, whose far light tints nearby smoke with the jet color) and the exhaust column, so with the canvas present the DOM jet light under each nozzle is hidden and takes over when the canvas is gone. It is a decorative `aria-hidden` canvas drawn behind the copy (inside the `container` when one is given), and it is not tied to the flight: it keeps dispersing after the layer is gone and the mark has appeared, then removes itself and releases its GL context (about 3 seconds after the last emission). It is also disposed when the component unmounts. It uses no Blob or worker, so a strict CSP does not matter. Without WebGL2 (or the float render extension) or under reduced motion the flight and the mark are the same, just without smoke. Turn it off with `smoke={false}`; the motion and the DOM jet light under each nozzle stay, only the smoke and the exhaust column go. Pressing again during the flight is ignored.

The original button stays in place but invisible, so the layout does not move. A `sentLabel` mark fades in on its spot (`settle`). It does **not** come back: change the `key` to render it again. There is no undo API.

It wraps `Button` primary strong (`md`), so it keeps the height, radius and press feel of `Button`. It has no `size` or `variant` prop.

```tsx
import { RocketButton } from '@taein-ui/core';

<RocketButton onClick={send} sentLabel="보냈어요" container={stageRef.current}>보내기</RocketButton>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| children | ReactNode | (required) | Button text and the accessible name |
| sentLabel | string | '보냈어요' | Text of the mark that appears where the button was |
| container | HTMLElement \| null | document.body | Where the flight layer is drawn. Given an element, the flight stays inside it and is clipped by it. It must be a `position` reference (`relative` and so on) and must not scroll |
| smoke | boolean | true | Fluid smoke that piles up on the virtual ground below the button during the build-up and the flight and trails weakly from under the nozzles during the launch, with the jet glow and exhaust column drawn by the same engine. `false` flies with the motion and the DOM jet light only |
| onClick | MouseEventHandler | - | Native click (on release). Called before the flight; `preventDefault()` there skips the flight. Never called on pointerdown (WCAG 2.5.2) |
| disabled | boolean | false | Disabled state; it does not crouch or fly |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the `<button>`) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLButtonElement> | - | Forwarded to the `<button>` |

Other native button attributes are passed to the `<button>`, except `children`. A `type="submit"` button submits on its first click as usual; after the flight there is no button to click again, and a click that still reaches the hidden button (implicit submission) is prevented.

### Accessibility
- The copy is `aria-hidden` and `inert` decoration (it loses its `id` and every `data-*` attribute).
- Focus: if the button had focus, it moves to the mark (`tabIndex=-1`) and the status region stays empty, because the text of a focused element is read and a status text would read it twice. If it had no focus, nothing moves and, once the flight is over, `sentLabel` is put into a visually hidden `role="status"` region that exists from the start (a region inserted together with its text may not be read).
- The nozzles and jet lights are inside the `aria-hidden`, `inert` copy, and the smoke canvas is `aria-hidden` and ignores the pointer. Turning the smoke off or lacking WebGL2 changes neither the announcement nor the focus.
- Reduced motion: no crouch, flight or smoke. The button cross-fades to the mark (`base`). The focus rule is the same.

---

## LuminousFlow

Background that fills its parent box: light strands (28) flow inside a winding river path and light motes (in proportion to the length: 48 per 2162 units) drift along it. It is drawn on a canvas 2D over an SVG atmosphere layer, and the flow speeds up with scroll (up to 3.3x, calming down when scrolling stops). The palette is fixed (cyan and blue on black) and there is no colour override API.

The root is `position: absolute; inset: 0`, so the parent must be a positioned box (`position: relative` or similar). The picture stays inside that box: the canvas is sized from the measured root box, so a small card works as well as a full screen.

```tsx
import { LuminousFlow } from '@taein-ui/core';

<div style={{ position: 'relative', height: 480 }}>
  <LuminousFlow paused={frozen} />
  {/* content on top stays clickable */}
</div>

// a tall box: the river gets more bends to cover it. Only the part near the visible window of the nearest
// scroll container (or the page window) is drawn, and the flow speed follows that scroll
<div style={{ height: 480, overflowY: 'auto' }}>
  <div style={{ position: 'relative', height: 3000 }}>
    <LuminousFlow />
  </div>
</div>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| paused | boolean | false | true stops the flow and keeps the current scene: there is no repeating draw loop, and one still frame is redrawn when the box size or the visible part changes. false continues without a jump in flow time. The pause control for WCAG 2.2.2 (a motion that lasts more than 5 seconds) |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class (on the root) |
| ref | Ref<HTMLDivElement> | - | Forwarded to the root `<div>` |

There is no `size`, `variant` or `disabled`. The river is scaled to the box width with one scale (the scene is 492 units wide), so it is never squashed. The box height decides the bend count: the smallest river whose height covers the box (a short box shows the top of the shortest river, and a longer box adds one bend per 520 units, up to 45 bends). The last bend leaves the box to the left when the bend count is even and to the right when it is odd. There is no prop for the direction; change the box length.

### Performance and CSP
- Drawing stops while the tab is hidden, the box is off screen (IntersectionObserver) or `paused` is true. Only a canvas of the box size is drawn (pixel ratio capped at 1 and by a pixel budget).
- The atmosphere layer (an SVG) is cached once per size as an image made from a Blob URL. A strict Content-Security-Policy therefore needs `img-src blob:`. Without canvas 2D the SVG layer simply stays visible.

### Accessibility
- The whole thing is decoration: the root is `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events: none`, with no focusable element.
- Reduced motion: one still frame (flow time 0), no flow, no drift.
- `paused` is the consumer's pause control. Give users a way to set it when the background is on screen longer than 5 seconds.

---

## ManuscriptFlip

Two-faced box whose cells flip one by one in writing order (left to right, top row to bottom row), revealing the back face. Flipping back runs the reverse order. A thin plain paper tile turns over each cell (`rotationY` 0 to 180, with perspective) and the cell's mask changes when its tile is halfway. `front` and `back` are free ReactNodes rendered once each, stacked in the same place and revealed by a `clip-path` mask on the two faces, so nothing is duplicated (no duplicate ids, no second copy of a focusable element). The consumer decides whether hover or press flips it: the component handles no events and only follows `flipped`.

```tsx
import { ManuscriptFlip } from '@taein-ui/core';

<ManuscriptFlip
  flipped={flipped}
  front={<img src="/shoe.jpg" alt="신발" />}
  back={<p>가볍고 오래 신는 러닝화입니다.</p>}
/>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| front | ReactNode | (required) | Front face. Rendered once |
| back | ReactNode | (required) | Back face. Rendered once |
| flipped | boolean | (required) | true shows the back face (controlled). A change flips the cells in writing order; if it changes mid-flip, the flip goes back from where it is |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class on the box. The box fills its parent's width, its height comes from the taller face or the consumer's class |
| ref | Ref<HTMLDivElement> | - | Forwarded to the root element |

It also takes the native div attributes except `children`. There is no `size` or `variant`. Do not give the box inner padding: the cell grid is laid over the box and would no longer match the faces (put padding inside the faces).

### Behavior
- Cells: the box is split from its measured size into whole columns and rows of about 48px per side, at most 48 cells (a bigger box gets bigger cells), and split again when the size changes (`ResizeObserver`). A box with no measurement yet (first render, SSR) has no tiles.
- Timing: one cell takes `base` (200ms) with `settle`. The whole flip is fixed at 700ms whatever the cell count: the start gap between cells is 500ms / (cells - 1), and a single cell takes 200ms. The cell's mask changes when it is halfway (100ms after its start), a discrete change, not per-frame layout. Only `transform` and `opacity` are animated.
- Mid-flip change: one timeline is played or reversed, so a change of `flipped` during a flip goes back from the current state in the opposite order, and the end is always the last intent.
- Faces: the face that is not shown is `inert` and `visibility: hidden`, so it is out of the accessibility tree and focus. While a flip runs, both faces are `inert` (nothing is half-clickable through the mask; a focused element in the face being left loses focus when the flip starts) and the shown face comes alive when the flip ends. The box itself is not a control and draws no focus ring. Focus rings inside a face are that content's own. Keep the button that flips it outside the box: if it sits inside a face, the focus on it is lost while the flip runs, and when the flip ends the focus is moved to the box (`tabIndex=-1`, `outline: none`) if it fell to `body`, so the next Tab goes into the new face. Focus that was outside the faces is never touched.
- First render (SSR included): the end state of `flipped`, one face visible, no tiles.
- Reduced motion: no cells or tiles. The two faces cross-fade (`base`, `settle`); the result (visible face, `inert`) is the same.
- The tiles layer is `aria-hidden`, takes no pointer events and is hidden in print.

---

## MorphingIcon

Icon that moves between two states. Its lines grow and fold into another shape by moving only their endpoints. `pair` picks one of five fixed pairs, `active` picks the state (false: the first icon of the pair, true: the second). It is one SVG sized `1em` and drawn in `currentColor`, so it takes the font size and color of the button around it and goes into `IconButton` as is. The state is told by that button (a fixed accessible name plus one state attribute (`aria-expanded` for menus and disclosures, `aria-pressed` for other toggles)), not by the icon.

```tsx
import { IconButton, MorphingIcon } from '@taein-ui/core';

<IconButton
  aria-label="메뉴"
  aria-expanded={open}
  onClick={() => setOpen((v) => !v)}
>
  <MorphingIcon pair="menu-close" active={open} />
</IconButton>
```

### Props
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| pair | 'menu-close' \| 'plus-check' \| 'play-pause' \| 'search-close' \| 'expand-collapse' | (required) | The two icons it moves between. Changing it on a mounted icon redraws from the new pair's shape |
| active | boolean | (required) | false shows the first icon of the pair (menu, plus, play, search, expand), true shows the second (close, check, pause, close, collapse). A change moves the endpoints; if it changes mid-move, the move goes on from the current coordinates |
| className | string | - | Additional CSS class on the SVG |
| ref | Ref<SVGSVGElement> | - | Forwarded to the SVG |

There is no `size` or `variant`: the size is `1em` and the color is `currentColor`. Set the size with the font size of the button or of a wrapper.

### Behavior
- Shape: every pair is drawn by hand as polylines in a 24 viewBox (stroke width 2, round caps and joins, no fill). Both states of a pair have the same number of lines and the same number of endpoints on each line, so the endpoints move one to one. A circle is approximated by 16 straight segments. A line that must vanish (the middle bar of the menu) shrinks to a single point and its opacity goes to 0 so the round cap does not stay as a dot.
- Motion: only endpoint coordinates (and opacity of vanishing lines) are tweened with GSAP, 300ms (`slow`) with `settle`. No MorphSVG or other plugin. The end coordinates equal the definition exactly.
- Mid-move change: the running tween is killed and a new one starts from the coordinates drawn at that moment, so the icon never jumps to an end shape.
- First render (SSR included): the shape of `active` drawn from the definition as is, no tween.
- Reduced motion: the shape changes at once to the end shape.
- Blue dots or other decoration: none. Only the lines change.

### Accessibility
- The SVG is `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`; the icon takes no focus.
- Put the state on the button around it: keep its accessible name fixed (`메뉴`) and set one state attribute, `aria-expanded` for a menu or disclosure, `aria-pressed` for other toggles (add, play, search). Do not also change the name with the state, or screen readers announce the state twice.

---

## Design Tokens

TUI uses `themeContract` for type-safe, theme-aware styling. 테마는 라이트
단일 테마 하나뿐이며 `:root`에 전역 CSS 변수로 선언된다. `ThemeProvider`,
`useTheme`, `createTheme`, 다크 테마는 존재하지 않는다. import하면 실패한다.

아래 값과 대비비는 모두 소스(`tokens/contract.ts`)에서 생성되므로 코드와
어긋날 수 없다.

### Color: Brand & Neutral

판정 기준은 흰 배경이 아니라 더 불리한 `background.paper`다.

- `themeContract.color.primary.main`: #1976D2, 4.60:1 on white / 4.40:1 on paper, AA UI only, not for body text
- `themeContract.color.primary.light`: #42A5F5, 2.64:1 on white / 2.53:1 on paper, decorative only, fails AA
- `themeContract.color.primary.dark`: #1565C0, 5.74:1 on white / 5.50:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.primary.contrast`: #FFFFFF, `primary.main` 위 글자색: 4.60:1
- `themeContract.color.text.primary`: #212121, 16.10:1 on white / 15.42:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.text.secondary`: #717171, 4.88:1 on white / 4.67:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.text.disabled`: #BDBDBD, 비활성 표시용. 대비가 낮으므로 색만으로 상태를 전달하지 않는다 (`disabled`/`aria-disabled`를 함께 쓴다)
- `themeContract.color.text.inverse`: #FFFFFF, 어두운 면 위 글자색 (Button·IconButton의 dark 변형, 스크림 위 텍스트)
- `themeContract.color.background.default`: #FFFFFF, 페이지 배경
- `themeContract.color.background.paper`: #FAFAFA, 카드·패널 배경. 대비 판정의 기준 배경이다
- `themeContract.color.surface.default`: #FFFFFF, 표면 기본
- `themeContract.color.surface.hover`: #F5F5F5, 표면 hover
- `themeContract.color.surface.active`: #EEEEEE, 표면 active
- `themeContract.color.surface.track`: #878787, 흰 배경 대비 3.59:1, 1.4.11의 3:1을 넘긴다. 컨트롤을 식별시키는 면(Switch·Slider의 트랙과 Loader `color="white"`의 트랙)에 쓴다. `border.strong`과 값은 같지만 경계선이 아니라 면이라 따로 둔다
- `themeContract.color.border.default`: #E0E0E0, 흰 배경 대비 1.32:1, UI 요소 기준 3:1 미달이므로 구분선·비활성 테두리처럼 정보를 전달하지 않는 자리에만 쓴다. 경계가 정보를 전달하면 `border.strong`
- `themeContract.color.border.strong`: #878787, 흰 배경 대비 3.59:1, 1.4.11의 3:1을 넘긴다. 폼 컨트롤·카드 경계처럼 있고 없고가 의미를 바꾸는 자리에 쓴다
- `themeContract.color.border.focus`: #1976D2, 포커스 링 색
- `themeContract.color.overlay.scrim`: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5), Modal·BottomSheet·SideSheet 백드롭. 반투명 합성색이라 단일 대비값이 없다
- `themeContract.color.overlay.focusHalo`: rgba(25, 118, 210, 0.16), 포커스 halo(장식). 실제 포커스 표시는 focusRing 유틸의 outline이 맡는다(TextField는 예외로 outline 없이 테두리 색이 맡는다)
- `themeContract.color.overlay.errorHalo`: rgba(211, 47, 47, 0.16), 에러 halo(장식). 위와 같은 이유로 포커스 표시를 겸하지 않는다

### Color: Semantic

Semantic 색상은 역할별 4슬롯이다. 슬롯을 바꿔 쓰면 대비가 깨진다:
- `main`: 글자(`contrast`)를 얹는 면. 판정 기준은 페이지 배경이 아니라
  `contrast`와의 대비 4.5:1이다. 배경과의 3:1은 보장 대상이 아니다
  (`success.main` 2.77, `warning.main` 2.15). **본문 텍스트로 쓰지 말 것**
- `light`: 연한 배경용. 위에는 `color.text.primary`를 얹는다
- `dark`: 흰 배경 위 본문 텍스트용 (기준 4.5:1). 글자를 얹지 않는 도형
  (아이콘 단독·차트 마커·상태 점)도 이 슬롯을 쓴다. 1.4.11의 3:1을 넘긴다
- `contrast`: `main` 위에 얹는 글자색

- `themeContract.color.success.main`: #4CAF50, 2.77:1 on white / 2.66:1 on paper, decorative only, fails AA
- `themeContract.color.success.light`: #C8E6C9, 배경용. 위에 `text.primary`를 얹으면 11.97:1
- `themeContract.color.success.dark`: #2E7D32, 5.12:1 on white / 4.91:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.success.contrast`: #212121, `success.main` 위 글자색: 5.79:1
- `themeContract.color.warning.main`: #FF9800, 2.15:1 on white / 2.06:1 on paper, decorative only, fails AA
- `themeContract.color.warning.light`: #FFE0B2, 배경용. 위에 `text.primary`를 얹으면 12.69:1
- `themeContract.color.warning.dark`: #A65200, 5.48:1 on white / 5.25:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.warning.contrast`: #212121, `warning.main` 위 글자색: 7.47:1
- `themeContract.color.error.main`: #D32F2F, 4.97:1 on white / 4.77:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.error.light`: #FFCDD2, 배경용. 위에 `text.primary`를 얹으면 11.43:1
- `themeContract.color.error.dark`: #C62828, 5.62:1 on white / 5.38:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.error.contrast`: #FFFFFF, `error.main` 위 글자색: 4.97:1
- `themeContract.color.info.main`: #1976D2, 4.60:1 on white / 4.40:1 on paper, AA UI only, not for body text
- `themeContract.color.info.light`: #BBDEFB, 배경용. 위에 `text.primary`를 얹으면 11.46:1
- `themeContract.color.info.dark`: #1565C0, 5.74:1 on white / 5.50:1 on paper, AA text
- `themeContract.color.info.contrast`: #FFFFFF, `info.main` 위 글자색: 4.60:1

`color.info`는 값이 `color.primary`와 같다(#1976D2). 의도한 것이며
정보 알림을 브랜드 블루로 표현한다. 그래도 `primary`를 빌려 쓰지 말고 `info`를
쓴다. 브랜드 색을 바꿀 때 알림 색이 따라 바뀌지 않으려면 어휘가 분리되어
있어야 한다.

### Color: Raw Palette
`themeContract.palette.{primary,gray,error,success,warning}[단계]`(정의된 단계만, 예: `warning`은 50·100·500·700·750·800): hover/active처럼 4슬롯으로
표현되지 않는 미세 단계가 필요할 때만 쓴다. 역할이 있는 자리에는 위의 역할
토큰을 쓴다.

### Spacing (8pt grid)
- `themeContract.spacing[n]`: 0 (0), 1 (0.25rem = 4px), 2 (0.5rem = 8px), 3 (0.75rem = 12px), 4 (1rem = 16px), 5 (1.25rem = 20px), 6 (1.5rem = 24px), 8 (2rem = 32px), 10 (2.5rem = 40px), 12 (3rem = 48px), 16 (4rem = 64px), 20 (5rem = 80px)
- 12단계에서 닫혀 있다. `spacing[7]`, `[9]`, `[11]`, `[13]`–`[15]`, `[17]`–`[19]`는
  정의되지 않았고 `undefined`를 반환한다. 최대값은 80px이다.

### Typography
- `font.family.sans`: "Pretendard Variable", Pretendard, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
- `font.family.mono`: "SF Mono", Monaco, "Cascadia Code", "Roboto Mono", Consolas, "Courier New", monospace
- `font.size`: 2xs (0.625rem = 10px), xs (0.75rem = 12px), sm (0.875rem = 14px), base (1rem = 16px), lg (1.125rem = 18px), xl (1.25rem = 20px), 2xl (1.5rem = 24px), 3xl (1.875rem = 30px), 4xl (2.25rem = 36px)
- `font.weight`: regular (400), medium (500), semibold (600), bold (700)
- `font.lineHeight`: tight (1.25), normal (1.5), relaxed (1.75)
- `font.variantNumeric`: normal (normal), tabular (tabular-nums)
  숫자를 세로로 비교하는 표·지표에는 `tabular`를 쓴다. 비례 폰트는 `1`이 `8`보다
  좁아서 자릿수가 행마다 어긋난다.

### Border Radius
- `themeContract.borderRadius`: none (0), sm (0.25rem = 4px), base (0.5rem = 8px), md (0.75rem = 12px), lg (1rem = 16px), xl (1.5rem = 24px), full (9999px)

### Shadow
- `themeContract.shadow`: none, sm, base, md, lg, xl, 2xl, inner

### Animation
- `animation.duration`: fast (150ms), base (200ms), slow (300ms), slower (500ms)
- `animation.loop`: fast (800ms), base (1500ms), slow (6000ms)
  전이(A→B)가 아니라 무한 반복 한 바퀴의 길이라 duration과 다른 양이다.
  같은 스케일에 끼우면 전이를 느리게 만드는 압력이 된다.
- `animation.easing`: settle (linear(0.0000,0.1565,0.2939,0.4138,0.5177,0.6072,0.6836,0.7483,0.8025,0.8474,0.8842,0.9139,0.9375,0.9559,0.9699,0.9802,0.9877,0.9928,0.9961,0.9981,0.9992,0.9998,1.0000,1.0000,1.0000)), snap (linear(0.0000,0.1849,0.3488,0.4928,0.6181,0.7258,0.8172,0.8934,0.9556,1.0049,1.0425,1.0697,1.0875,1.0972,1.0998,1.0967,1.0889,1.0776,1.0641,1.0494,1.0347,1.0213,1.0102,1.0028,1.0000)), spring (linear(0.0000,0.3512,0.7194,1.0000,1.1575,1.2044,1.1768,1.1147,1.0496,1.0000,0.9722,0.9639,0.9688,0.9797,0.9912,1.0000,1.0049,1.0064,1.0055,1.0036,1.0016,1.0000,0.9991,0.9989,1.0000)), exit (linear(0.0000,0.0001,0.0006,0.0020,0.0046,0.0090,0.0156,0.0248,0.0370,0.0527,0.0723,0.0963,0.1250,0.1589,0.1985,0.2441,0.2963,0.3554,0.4219,0.4962,0.5787,0.6699,0.7703,0.8801,1.0000)), linear (linear(0.0000,0.0417,0.0833,0.1250,0.1667,0.2083,0.2500,0.2917,0.3333,0.3750,0.4167,0.4583,0.5000,0.5417,0.5833,0.6250,0.6667,0.7083,0.7500,0.7917,0.8333,0.8750,0.9167,0.9583,1.0000)), drift (linear(0.0000,0.0043,0.0170,0.0381,0.0670,0.1033,0.1464,0.1956,0.2500,0.3087,0.3706,0.4347,0.5000,0.5653,0.6294,0.6913,0.7500,0.8044,0.8536,0.8967,0.9330,0.9619,0.9830,0.9957,1.0000))
- **토큰 경계**: 여러 컴포넌트가 공유하는 의미(전이 속도, 반복 주기,
  등장·퇴장 커브)만 토큰이다. 한 컴포넌트에만 있는 연출의 내부 타이밍
  (Skeleton wave 시작 지연, Loader 점 스태거 같은 delay)은 토큰이 아니고,
  그래도 duration·loop 토큰의 배수로 적는다. `.css.ts`에 duration을 리터럴로 박지 않는다.
- 오버슈트 이징 `snap`(피크 1.0998)·`spring`(피크 1.2044)은 `transform`에만 건다.
  값이 1을 넘어야 튕김이 보이는데 `opacity`·색은 1에서 잘려 인공물만 남는다.
- `transition: all`을 쓰지 않는다. 전이할 속성을 적는다. 합성·페인트 속성
  (transform/opacity/filter/색/box-shadow/text-shadow) 밖을 전이하려면 근거를 남긴다.
- 이 경계는 `src/tokens/animationBoundary.test.ts`가 소스 스캔으로 잠근다.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`이면 duration 넷과 loop 셋, 일곱 개가 모두 `0.01ms`로
  덮어써지고, 전역 규칙이 `*, *::before, *::after`의 animation/transition duration·delay와
  반복 횟수까지 함께 내린다. 토큰을 안 쓰고 초를 리터럴로 박은 애니메이션
  (Skeleton의 무한 wave/pulse 등)도 멈춘다.

### Z-Index
- `themeContract.zIndex`: base (0), dropdown (1000), sticky (1100), overlay (1200), modal (1300), popover (1400), toast (1500), tooltip (1600)
- 층 이름으로 참조한다. 숫자를 직접 쓰면 소비자가 자기 오버레이를 안전하게
  얹을 값을 알 수 없다.
- `sticky` HeaderBar · `overlay` 배경 딤 · `modal` Modal/BottomSheet/SideSheet/
  Loader(fullScreen) · `popover` Popover · `toast` Snackbar · `tooltip` Tooltip.
- `popover`/`tooltip`/`toast`가 `modal`보다 위인 것은 의도다. 모달 안에서 툴팁을
  띄우거나 모달 위에 Snackbar를 올리는 조합이 흔하다.

### Breakpoints
- `breakpoint`: sm (360px), md (768px), lg (1024px), xl (1280px)
- `mediaQuery.up.md`: `screen and (min-width: 768px)`
- `mediaQuery.down.md`: `screen and (max-width: 767.98px)`
- `themeContract`에 없다. CSS 변수는 `@media` 조건에서 동작하지 않으므로
  (`@media (min-width: var(--x))`는 무효) 브레이크포인트는 빌드 타임 상수이며
  테마로 바꿀 수 없다. `mediaQuery`를 import해 `.css.ts`의 `@media` 키에 그대로
  넣는다. `down`이 1px이 아니라 0.02px을 빼는 것은 소수 픽셀 폭에서 `up`과
  사이에 틈이 생기지 않게 하기 위함이다.

## Motion (GSAP Runtime)

GSAP 런타임(M3 Tier-B에서 시작해 M7까지)에서 실제로 GSAP이 붙은 컴포넌트와 그 능력이다. 계획서의
예측이 아니라 구현된 소스에서 읽었다. 아래에 없는 컴포넌트는 GSAP을 쓰지 않는다(CSS 트랜지션·키프레임을 쓰고,
`LuminousFlow`는 canvas 그리기 루프를, `SloshGauge`는 rAF 루프로 SVG를 고쳐 쓴다). 공유 easing·duration 토큰은 위 Design Tokens > Animation 절 참고.

| 컴포넌트 | 쓰는 능력 | 근거 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Modal | 타임라인 상대 위치 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(트리거 좌표) | 백드롭·다이얼로그를 한 타임라인에 넣고, `triggerStart`가 두 사각형 차이와 container 배율로 시작 x/y·clip-path·배경색을 읽는다. 닫을 때 트리거의 현재 값을 다시 읽는다 |
| BottomSheet | 타임라인 상대 위치 · 제스처 추적(터치 드래그 1:1) | 등장·퇴장은 `useOverlayTransition`, 터치 드래그는 `gsap.quickSetter(sheet, 'y', 'px')`로 손가락을 1:1로 따라간다 |
| SideSheet | 타임라인 상대 위치 | `useOverlayTransition`만 쓴다. 직접 `gsap` import도, 트리거 좌표도, 드래그도 없다 |
| Snackbar | CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(카운트다운 진행률 read-back) · 같은 위치 쌓임 오프셋(`y`, base settle) | `gsap.to(proxy, { remaining: 0, ... })`의 `remaining` 값 자체를 막대 렌더와 닫힘 판정이 함께 읽는다. CSS/WAAPI로는 진행률을 밖에서 못 읽는다. 유일한 GATE_ENFORCEMENT_EXCEPTIONS 항목이다. 같은 위치 쌓임 오프셋은 등장 타임라인과 따로 시트의 `y`를 `gsapDuration.base` `settle`로 트윈하고 `gateMotion`을 거친다(축소 선호면 즉시) |
| Checkbox | 모양 변형(checked ↔ indeterminate) · 다중 목표 중단 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(스프링 진행값 하나로 채움·상자 구동) | `MorphSVGPlugin`으로 체크 표시 경로를 모핑한다. 체크·해제는 진행값 `t`(0↔1)를 트윈하고 `onUpdate`가 채움 층 `scale(max(t, 0))`과 상자 `scale(1 + 0.35 × max(0, t - 1))`를 쓰고, 획 `strokeDashoffset`은 스프링을 따르지 않고 같은 타임라인의 자기 트윈(`slow` `settle`)으로 그어진다. 스프링이 1을 넘는 순간에만 상자가 부푼다. 체크와 해제 모두 두 번째 진행값 `s`가 1 → 0.88(`base` `drift`)로 상자를 먼저 안으로 움츠렸다가 `base` 시점에 1로 `slower` `spring`으로 되튀고, 체크는 이때 채움·부풂(`slower` `spring`)과 획 트윈이 같이 시작해 채움이 터진다(해제는 파란색이 빨려 들어간 뒤 되튄다). 상자 scale은 부풂 × `s`로 합성해 한 곳에서만 쓴다. 도중에 반대로 바뀌면 트윈을 죽이고 지금 `t`·`s`·획에서 새 목표로 다시 트윈한다. checked ↔ indeterminate 모프는 `t`와 `s`가 1이 아니면 1로 돌려 상자가 틀어진 크기로 남지 않게 한다 |
| Switch | 타임라인 상대 위치 · 다중 목표 중단 | 이동 하나를 진행값 `p`(`slow` `drift`, 300ms)로 트윈하고, 머리 x · 늘임 `1 + 0.144 × sin(π p)`(가로에 곱하고 세로에 나눠 부피 보존) · 파란 채움이 같은 `p`를 따른다(채움은 트랙 알약 모양으로 자르는 칸 안의 직사각형이라 차오르는 도중에도 트랙 밖으로 나가지 않는다). 늘임은 이동 속도에서만 나오고 출발 전 늘임은 없다. 켜진 머리 크기는 `(트랙 높이 + 2) / 머리 크기`(`md` 1.3)이고 이동 80% 시점에 `base` `drift`로 바뀌어 켜짐이면 그 크기로 머물고 꺼짐이면 1로 돌아온다. 도중에 반대로 바뀌면 지금 x · 크기 · 늘임에서 이어진다(늘임 초과분을 `1 - p`로 줄여 간다). 호버 부풂(1.06)은 GSAP이 쓰는 머리 칸이 아니라 안쪽 면의 CSS라 서로 곱해져 합성된다 |
| SegmentedButtons | 타임라인 상대 위치 · 다중 목표 중단 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(인디케이터 좌표) | 표시는 트랙 전체 폭의 층을 `clip-path: inset(...)`으로 잘라 그리고, 두 가장자리 L·R(트랙 왼쪽 기준 px)을 트윈한다(`scaleX`로 늘이지 않아 둥근 끝이 납작해지지 않는다). 옮겨 가면 한 타임라인이 다섯 단계를 돈다. 두 가장자리가 옛 칸과 새 칸을 함께 덮도록 벌어지고(`base` `settle`), `fast` 뒤 앞 가장자리가 새 칸 끝에 앉으며(`slow` `settle`), 뒤 가장자리가 새 칸 끝을 3px 지나쳤다가(`slow` `settle`) 제자리로 돌아온다(`fast` `settle`). 그림자는 자르는 층이 아니라 그 부모의 `drop-shadow`가 그린다. 글자색은 표시 가장자리에서 갈린다: 표시 층 안에 진짜 라벨과 같은 클래스·배치의 라벨 줄을 한 벌 더(`aria-hidden`, 활성색) 그리고 표시 층을 진짜 라벨 위에 쌓으며, 진짜 라벨의 글자색은 선택과 무관하게 늘 비활성색이다. 고무는 선택 값이 바뀔 때만 돌고 값이 같은데 칸 좌표만 바뀌면 새 자리에 바로 앉는다. 선택마다 새 타임라인을 만들고(재사용 금지) 이전 타임라인은 죽이며 새 타임라인이 가장자리의 지금 값에서 이어받는다. 칸 위치는 `selectedLabel`/컨테이너의 `getBoundingClientRect()`로 잰다 |
| NumericSpinner | 다중 목표 중단 | 버튼과 칸 안의 숫자(`<input>`, 숫자 칸 상자는 가만히 있다)가 함께 눌리는 깊이(2단 타임라인, 버튼 0.90에서 0.86, 숫자 0.82에서 0.76. 떼면 그 타임라인을 죽이고 지금 자리에서 버튼 1.06, 숫자 1.12까지 부풀었다 1로 내려앉는 타임라인 하나)와 입력 필드 흔들림(`gsap.fromTo(..., { overwrite: 'auto' })`) 두 채널 모두 재호출을 안전하게 흡수한다 |
| Slider | 제스처 추적(드래그 중 값 따라붙기) · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(`wake`의 머리 속도) | 값이 한 번에 바뀌어도(트랙 클릭, 키보드, 큰 `step`) 머리와 채움이 약 0.3초 스프링으로 이동한다: 보이는 위치를 GSAP ticker 안에서 임계 감쇠 스프링으로 값에 따라가게 하고(트윈이 아니라 물리 적분이라 길이·커브 토큰이 아니다) 그린 머리, 채움(`clipPath`, `wake`의 켜진 막대), 값 따라붙기(`VALUE_FOLLOWER_PERCENT_VAR`)가 모두 이것을 따른다. 포인터로 끄는 동안은 한 단계 폭이 12px 이하면 목표를 그대로 쓰고(누른 순간의 첫 점프는 스프링) 12px보다 넓은 큰 `step` 스냅은 늘 스프링이며, 축소 선호에서는 바로 이동한다. `variant="wake"`에서는 머리 위치를 GSAP ticker 안에서 임계 감쇠 스프링으로 값에 따라가게 하고 그 속도를 과감쇠 스프링으로 걸러(둘 다 트윈이 아니라 물리 적분이라 길이·커브 토큰이 아니다) 세기를 재, 막대 `scaleY`에 끄는 세기에 비례하고 서서히 차오르는 `cos²` 물결을 쓴다(세기는 960px/s에서 최대)(축소 선호에서는 ticker를 붙이지 않는다). `default`·`bar`는 같은 머리 추적과 ticker로 라인 SVG 경로의 두께 함수에 같은 물결을 쓰고(끌면 머리 둘레 선이 속도에 비례해 부풀어 물결치고 뒤쪽으로 길게 퍼지며 멈추면 매끈해진다), 호버 두께는 마우스에서만 `gsap.to`(들어갈 때 `slow` `spring`, 나올 때 `base` `settle`)가 바탕 두께를 옮긴다 |
| HeaderBar | 제스처 추적(`navStyle="icon"`의 커서가 올라간 항목 확대) · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(알약 크기, 카드 층 높이) · 다중 목표 중단(768px 미만 메뉴 판, `navStyle="dropdown"`의 하위 링크 판) · 멈춘 타임라인 재생(`navStyle="pill"`, `navStyle="cards"`) | `navStyle="icon"`은 `pointerenter`·`focus`한 항목만 `gsap.quickTo` 세터로 `MAX_SCALE`까지 키우고 나머지는 1로 둔다. 좁은 화면 메뉴 판은 `autoAlpha`(opacity + visibility)와 `y`를 `gsap.to`로 열 때 `base` `settle`(`0 → 1`, `y 8 → 0`), 닫을 때 `fast` `settle`로 트윈하고 `overwrite: 'auto'`라 도중에 뒤집으면 지금 자리에서 이어진다. 둘 다 `gateMotion`/`settleMotion`을 거친다. `navStyle="cards"`는 면 `height`와 카드 `y`·`opacity`를 멈춘 타임라인 하나(`slow` `settle`, 시차 80ms, 카드는 면 트윈의 3/4 지점에서 시작)로 묶어 열 때 `play()`, 닫을 때 `reverse()`로 재생하고, 축소 선호에서는 끝·처음으로 바로 간다 |
| Avatar | 다중 목표 중단(떠오름과 눌림이 서로를 덮어쓰며 이어짐) | 호버·포커스의 떠오름(`yPercent`)과 누름의 `scale`이 각자 `overwrite: 'auto'`로 지금 자리에서 새 목표로 이어진다. 호버는 spring, 되돌아올 때는 settle이다 |
| BoardRow | 타임라인 상대 위치 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(트윈 중간 높이, 내용 높이) | 펼침은 `height`를 현재 높이에서 `scrollHeight`보다 살짝 넘겼다가 내용 높이로 되돌리는 두 구간 타임라인이고, 접힘은 부풀었다가 0으로 간다. 도중에 뒤집으면 죽이기 전에 읽은 중간 높이에서 출발한다 |
| Chip | 타임라인 상대 위치 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(폭과 gap으로 자리 닫기) | 삭제는 두 구간이다. 먼저 `scale`·`opacity`가 0으로 빨려 들어가고, 이어서 `marginInlineEnd`를 `-(offsetWidth + columnGap)`으로 줘 자리를 닫아 오른쪽 칩이 미끄러져 온다. `onDelete`는 타임라인이 끝난 뒤 불린다 |
| IconButton | 타임라인 상대 위치 | 기본으로 켜져 있고 `hoverEffect="none"`으로 끈다. 마우스가 들어오면 아이콘 칸이 두 구간 타임라인을 돈다. 먼저 `scaleX`가 1.15로, `scaleY`가 그 역수로 퍼지고(부피 보존), 이어서 둘이 1로 spring 커브를 타고 1을 지나쳤다가 앉는다. 도는 중에 다시 들어오면 무시한다 |
| Loader | 타임라인 상대 위치 · 다중 목표 중단 | `type="orbit"`의 `status`가 `done`·`error`로 바뀌면 점 8개가 한 타임라인에서 각도순으로 짝지은 체크·X 자리로 모인다(점마다 `fast / 8` 시차, `slow` `settle`). `loading`으로 돌아오면 같은 길로 원 위에 돌아가 도착한 뒤에 밝기 키프레임이 재개되고, 도중에 바뀌면 점의 지금 위치에서 이어간다. 라벨 글자가 바뀌면 타임라인 하나가 두 글자 층을 흐림으로 교체한다(옛 층 투명도 0·`blur(2px)`, 새 층 0·`blur(2px)`에서 1·`blur(0)`, `base` `settle`). 켜지지 않은 층은 절대 위치(`left: 0; right: 0`)라 칸 폭에 들어가지 않고, 타임라인이 끝나거나 죽으면 옛 층은 글자를 비운다. 칸 폭은 새 글자 기준으로 그 커밋에 바로 바뀌고 트윈하지 않는다. 라벨이 칸 폭을 정하는 배치(내용 폭으로 줄어들고 한쪽에 붙은 자리)에서는 그래픽도 그때 한 번 옮겨 가므로, 라벨이 바뀌는 로더는 가운데 정렬 자리에 둔다. 라벨 교체는 레이아웃을 읽지 않는다 |
| HangulAssemble | 타임라인 상대 위치 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(폰트 대기용 computed font) | 오린 조각 전체를 타임라인 하나에 시차(`staggerStep`, 음절 안은 `PIECE_STAGGER`)로 넣고, 조각이 `slower` `settle`로 흩어진 자리에서 제자리로 날아온 순간 조각 층을 걷고 완성 글자를 드러낸다(교차 페이드 없음). 흩어진 자리는 px 단위(60~120px)다. 재생 전에 `document.fonts.load`로 폰트를 기다린다(3초 상한). 축소 선호에서는 `gateMotion`이 끝 상태(완성 글자)로 확정한다 |
| BrushText | 타임라인 상대 위치 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(폰트 대기용 computed font, 캔버스로 잰 잉크) | 획마다 진행값 하나를 `linear`로 트윈하고 `onUpdate`가 앞머리까지의 픽셀만 다시 쓴다. 획 시작 시각과 길이는 순수 함수 `brushSchedule`이 정한다(획은 길이에 비례해 1em에 `base`, 최소 `fast` * 0.4. 쉼은 같은 자모 안 `fast` * 0.4, 자모 사이 `base` * 0.5, 음절 사이 `fast`. 상한 없음). 칸의 마지막 획이 끝나는 순간 캔버스를 숨기고 완성 글자를 드러낸다. 쓰기 전에 `document.fonts.load`로 폰트를 기다린다(3초 상한). 축소 선호에서는 `gateMotion`이 끝 상태(완성 글자)로 확정한다 |
| BurstToggle | 타임라인 상대 위치 · 다중 목표 중단 | 켜면 점들이 사방으로 `slower` `settle`로 퍼지는 타임라인과, 아이콘 칸이 납작했다 튕기는 타임라인(`fast` `settle`로 시작)이 따로 돈다. 새 터짐이 서면 이전 아이콘 칸 타임라인을 죽이고 새로 만든다. 켜짐 상태는 소비자가 쥔다 |
| HoldButton | 다중 목표 중단 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(홀드 진행값) | 진행값 `p`(0~1) 하나를 `gsap.to`로 트윈하고(홀드 시계, 선형), `onUpdate`가 채움을 그린다. 이 시계는 `gateMotion`을 거치지 않는다(축소 모드에서 즉시 실행되면 안 되므로 `GATE_ENFORCEMENT_EXCEPTIONS` 항목, 축소 모드는 그림만 단계로 끊는다). 놓으면 시계를 죽이고 지금 `p`에서 0으로 `base` `settle`로 되감는다. 끝 무렵의 떨림은 시계와 분리된 장식 타임라인(게이트를 거친다)이다 |
| CodeSlots | 단일 트윈(숫자가 굴러 들어옴, 지우면 빠짐) + 성공 합쳐짐 타임라인 하나 | 숫자가 들어오면 `yPercent -100 → 0`(`base` `snap`)으로 굴러 들어오고, 지우면 `0 → 100`(`base` `exit`)으로 빠진 뒤 `onComplete`가 빠짐을 확정한다. 슬롯 하나가 트윈 하나씩 갖고 정리 때 죽인다. 성공 합쳐짐은 칸 줄의 CSS 숫자 둘(`fade` 1 → 0 `base` `settle`, 이어서 `merge` 0 → 1 `slower` `settle`)을 모는 타임라인 하나이고, 성공이 켜지면 `play`, 풀리면 `reverse`한다. 정리 때 죽이고 인라인 숫자를 걷는다. 움직임 줄이기에서는 타임라인 없이 CSS가 끝 모양을 세운다 |
| RocketButton | 타임라인 상대 위치 · 다중 목표 중단 · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(단추·container 좌표) | 누르는 순간 웅크림을 `fast` `settle`로 트윈하고(`overwrite: true`) 떼거나 나가면 `base` `settle`로 되돌려, 웅크리는 도중에 풀려도 지금 값에서 이어진다. 발사하면 단추 좌표와 `container` 좌표(`getBoundingClientRect()`)를 읽어 발사 거리를 만들고 `document.body`의 비행 레이어에서 타임라인 하나가 시계 숫자를 0에서 5300ms까지 돌리며 `onUpdate`마다 로켓 박자 함수(분사구·분출·발사·표지)를 평가해 단추의 움직임과 분출 세기, 심지 길이(`scaleY`)를 놓고 가상의 땅과 분출구 아래의 연기 궤적을 낸다. 축소 선호에서는 단추와 표지가 교차 페이드한다 |
| ManuscriptFlip | 타임라인 상대 위치 · play/reverse(도중 되넘김) · CSS가 못 보는 값 읽기(타임라인 시각으로 마스크 칸 수 계산) | 칸 타일마다 `rotationY` 0에서 180을 `base` `settle`로 도는 트윈(투명도는 앞뒤 `base`의 4분의 1씩 `linear`)을 칸 순서대로 시작 시각만 달리해 타임라인 하나에 놓는다(전체 700ms). `onUpdate`가 타임라인 시각에서 "반쯤 돈 칸 수"를 세어 그 수가 바뀔 때만 두 면의 `clip-path`를 쓴다. `flipped`가 바뀌면 같은 타임라인을 `play`/`reverse`한다(시간 0에서의 되넘김은 `pause(0)`로 마무리). 움직임 줄이기는 두 면의 `opacity` 교차 흐림 타임라인(`base` `settle`) |
| MorphingIcon | 단일 트윈(선 끝점 좌표 숫자들을 한 번에 옮김) · 다중 목표 중단(도중 전환은 지금 좌표에서 새 목표로) |

**Flip은 이 목록 어디에도 없다.** 유일한 후보였던 `Card`는 레이아웃 변화를
CSS 전환으로 충분히 표현할 수 있다고 판단해 채택하지 않았다.

## Next.js & Server Components

### 설치

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import '@taein-ui/core/styles.css';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="ko">
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

`styles.css`는 루트 레이아웃에서 한 번만 import한다. Vanilla Extract는
zero-runtime이라 빌드 결과는 정적 CSS 파일 하나다.

### 'use client'

훅이나 컨텍스트를 쓰는 모듈에는 빌드 시 `'use client'`가 자동으로 주입된다.
소비자가 래퍼 파일을 만들 필요 없이 서버 컴포넌트에서 바로 import할 수 있다.

`Divider`, `Border`, `List`, `Skeleton`은 지시문이 없다. 서버 컴포넌트로 렌더된다.

`Button`과 `IconButton`은 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 누름 상태를 `useClickRebound` 훅이
갖기 때문이다. 서버 컴포넌트에서 import하는 것은 그대로 되고, `onClick` 같은 함수
prop은 클라이언트 파일에서 넘긴다.

`Badge`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 값이 바뀔 때 헌 값을 남겨 두고 교체 모션을 돌리는 상태(`useState`)를 갖는다.

`Loader`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. GSAP 트윈으로 그려서 브라우저에서만 돈다.

`HangulAssemble`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 화면에 들어올 때를 보는 관찰자와 GSAP 타임라인이 브라우저에서만 돈다.
첫 렌더(서버 포함)는 완성 문장이라 하이드레이션 전에도 글자가 보인다.

`BrushText`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 화면에 들어올 때를 보는 관찰자와 GSAP 타임라인이 브라우저에서만 돈다.
첫 렌더(서버 포함)는 완성 문장이라 하이드레이션 전에도 글자가 보인다.

`ManuscriptFlip`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 상자 크기를 관찰하고 GSAP 타임라인을 돌려 브라우저에서만 돈다. 첫 렌더(서버 포함)는 `flipped` 값대로 한 면만 보이는 끝 모양이고 타일이 없다. `flipped`는 소비자가 쥐므로 그 상태를 가진 클라이언트 파일에서 렌더한다.

`MorphingIcon`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 끝점을 옮기는 GSAP 트윈을 효과에서 돌려 브라우저에서만 돈다. 첫 렌더(서버 포함)는 `active`대로 짝의 한 모양을 그대로 그린 SVG다. `active`는 소비자가 쥐므로 그 상태를 가진 클라이언트 파일에서 렌더한다.

`GooeySearch`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 바깥 pointerdown과 Esc를 문서에서 듣고 포커스를 옮기는 효과를 갖는다.
열림 상태는 소비자가 쥐므로 그 상태를 가진 클라이언트 파일에서 렌더한다.

`CopyButton`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 결과 상태와 되돌림 타이머를 갖고 클릭에서 클립보드를 쓴다.

`BurstToggle`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 터짐 상태를 갖고 클릭에서 GSAP 타임라인을 돌린다. 켜짐 상태는 소비자가 쥐므로 그 상태를 가진 클라이언트 파일에서 렌더한다.

`SloshGauge`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. rAF 루프로 SVG 수면을 그려 브라우저에서만 돈다(GSAP은 쓰지 않는다). 표시 요소라 함수 prop은 없다.

`CodeSlots`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 값과 지워진 숫자의 빠짐 상태를 갖고 입력 이벤트에서 돈다. `onChange`·`onComplete` 같은 함수 prop은 클라이언트 파일에서 넘긴다.

`FanMenu`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 열림·가리킴·포커스 상태를 갖고 포인터와 키보드 이벤트에서 돈다. `items`의 `onSelect` 같은 함수 prop은 클라이언트 파일에서 넘긴다.

`RocketButton`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 날아갔는지의 상태를 갖고 포인터·클릭 이벤트에서 GSAP 타임라인을 돌리며 `document.body`에 비행 레이어를 그린다. `onClick` 같은 함수 prop과 `container`(DOM 요소)는 클라이언트 파일에서 넘긴다.

`LuminousFlow`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. canvas 그리기·스크롤 구독·관찰자를 브라우저에서만 돌린다. 첫 렌더(서버 포함)는 대기층 SVG와 어두운 바탕이다. `paused` 같은 prop은 직렬화되는 값이라 서버 컴포넌트에서 넘겨도 된다.

`HoldButton`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 홀드 시계(GSAP 트윈)와 무장·실행 상태를 갖고 포인터와 키보드 이벤트에서 돈다. `onConfirm` 같은 함수 prop은 클라이언트 파일에서 넘긴다.

`HeaderBar`도 `'use client'`가 붙는다. 좁은 화면 메뉴의 열림 상태와 GSAP 트윈,
그리고 `navStyle="icon"`의 항목 확대가 브라우저에서만 돈다.

`TextField`는 `'use client'`가 붙는다. `multiline`의 `autoResize`가 높이를 읽고 쓰는 훅을 갖는다.

단, 서버 컴포넌트에서 `onClick` 같은 함수 prop을 넘기는 것은 TUI와 무관하게
React가 막는다. 이벤트 핸들러를 붙이는 파일 쪽에 `'use client'`를 적어야 한다.

### 하이드레이션

테마 플래시가 없다. 테마가 라이트 단일이고 `:root`의 정적 CSS 변수로 선언되므로
하이드레이션 전후로 색이 바뀌지 않고, 테마 결정 스크립트나 `suppressHydrationWarning`,
쿠키·localStorage 읽기가 필요 없다. 다크 테마와 `ThemeProvider`는 존재하지 않는다.

---

## Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

All components follow WCAG 2.2 AA standards:
- Semantic HTML elements (button, input, dialog, etc.)
- ARIA attributes (aria-label, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-busy, aria-modal, aria-expanded)
- Keyboard navigation (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Escape, Arrow keys)
- Focus indicators (2px outline, 2px offset, 4.6:1 contrast ratio for buttons and cards; the input controls Checkbox, Switch, Slider, NumericSpinner, GooeySearch, SegmentedButtons and Chip show focus on their own border instead)
- Focus traps in overlays (Modal, BottomSheet, SideSheet)
- Screen reader announcements via aria-live regions

### Color contrast

- 본문 텍스트 4.5:1, UI 요소 3:1 기준. 토큰별 실측값은 Design Tokens 절에 있고
  소스에서 생성되므로 문서와 코드가 어긋날 수 없다.
- 판정은 흰 배경이 아니라 더 불리한 `background.paper`(#FAFAFA) 기준이다.
  Card 안에서 조용히 기준을 밑도는 것을 막기 위함이다.
- semantic 색의 `main` 슬롯은 UI 요소용이다. 본문 텍스트에는 `dark` 슬롯을 쓴다.

### Target size

- **WCAG 2.2 AA(2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum))의 요구치는 24x24 CSS px이다.**
  흔히 인용되는 44x44는 AA 기준이 아니라 AAA(2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced))에
  가까운 값이다.
- TUI는 인터랙티브 컴포넌트에 기본으로 44x44를 확보한다(AA 하한선보다 여유 있는
  자체 권장치). 좁은 화면에서 줄여야 한다면 24x24가 AA를 유지하는 하한이다.

### Reduced motion

- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`에서 두 겹으로 처리된다.
  1. `animation`의 duration 넷과 loop 셋, 일곱 개 변수가 모두 `0.01ms`로
     덮어써진다. 토큰을 쓰는 컴포넌트와, 그 토큰을 참조하는 소비자 스타일이
     함께 따라온다.
  2. 전역 규칙이 `*, *::before, *::after`에 여섯 줄을 `!important`로 건다:
     `animation-duration` · `animation-delay` · `transition-duration` ·
     `transition-delay`를 `0.01ms`로, `animation-iteration-count`를 `1`로,
     `scroll-behavior`를 `auto`로 내린다. 토큰을 안 쓰고 초를 리터럴로 박은
     애니메이션도 여기서 멈춘다.
- 2번이 필요한 이유는 무한 반복 애니메이션이다. `Skeleton`의 wave/pulse는
  `infinite`라 duration만 줄이면 더 빨리 깜빡일 뿐 멈추지 않는다.
- GSAP으로 움직이는 컴포넌트(Motion 절 참고)는 위 두 겹으로 못 잡는다.
  인라인 스타일로 도는 트윈이라 전역 CSS 규칙이 안 닿는다. 그래서 각 컴포넌트가
  훅 안에서 `useReducedMotion()`으로 같은 선호를 직접 확인하고, `gateMotion`이
  트윈을 끝 상태로 확정한 뒤 끈다(`hooks/gateMotion.ts`). 중간 상태에 멈추는
  프레임이 구조적으로 없다.
